definition-changed.answer: The rule speaks of a declarative (USE) procedure, which is a declarative section in both editions; §2002:4 (entry 4.150) already covers one section ('one or more successive ... sections'), and §2023:3.145 only spells out the single paragraph/section case. Same units, scope unchanged. 'a declarative procedure for which the GLOBAL phrase is specified' is the USE GLOBAL section in both.

pending-clause.answer: Read §2002:14.5.12.1.1 through §2002:14.5.12.2 against §2023:14.6.13.1.1 through §2023:14.6.13.2. The 2002 differences are: no MERGE/SORT, fatal-EC-I-O or PERFORM WHEN steps in fatal processing (§2023:14.6.13.1.3 (items 2-4) are 2023-only), the 2002 non-fatal wording, and the incompatible-data text. SR1 is a compile-time placement rule (no GOBACK written in a GLOBAL declarative); it names no exception condition and does not depend on how exceptions are processed. The refusals at --std 2002 (COBOL2102 for program, function and method) stand.
